text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service `inference-gateway-us-east` (HIGH). Incident ID: INC-82419. Trigger: 5xx spike on /v1/generate — 30% error rate across regional load balancer. PagerDuty: https://pd.example/INC-82419
PagerDuty: Auto-escalation started, notifying primary on-call for inference (Maya Patel).
Maya Patel: acked. I'm on the page, jumping in. tagging @Samir for infra assist. Please post any immediate checks you run.
Samir Khan: ack. I will pull pod logs and check node GPU utilization. Quick check: are we seeing OOMs or API gateway errors?
Jill Romero: saw customer report in SRE-monitoring: several enterprise tenants getting 503s and retries. Customer Impact: degraded generation latency -> failed requests. Ticket linked: https://support.redwood/internal/INC-82419-custs
Maya Patel: initial quick probe: ingress spike + increases in queue length on worker pool. No global cpu saturation. Adding runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-5xx-spike
Samir Khan: running commands now:
```bash
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference-worker -o wide
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=inference-worker --tail=200 | grep -i oom
```
Samir Khan: found repeated OOMKilled on node gpu-23 (container: worker-quantize). Eviction events spike around the alert window.
Maya Patel: good find. Rolling restart worker pool on gpu-23 and draining node for inspection. Can we reduce batch size/worker concurrency for the pool as temporary mitigation?
Samir Khan: deploying a temporary config that lowers max_batch_size and concurrency for the impacted pool. Patch applied to canary subset. Command: `kubectl -n inference set env deploy/worker-pool MAX_BATCH=8 MAX_CONCURRENCY=4 --record`
Leo Wong: FYI I'm watching customer-facing metrics. I'll flip failover to eu-west for high-priority tenants if canary doesn't improve within 10m.
Jill Romero: posting a customer-impact note in the incident tracker and pinging AMs for affected tenants. Draft message: "We're investigating increased 5xx errors on generation endpoints; teams are mitigating and we'll share updates every 10m."
incident-bot: Update: PagerDuty notes updated. Escalation level remains high until error rate < 1% sustained for 5m.
Maya Patel: canary shows 50% reduction in 5xx rate on the canary pool after lowering batch size. Still seeing some residual errors. Moving to wider rollout of reduced concurrency. Handing primary ownership to Samir — I have a blocker meeting in 6m. Samir, can you take point and post status every 10m?
Samir Khan: taking ownership. I'll post status pings. Next update in 5m.
Samir Khan: (5m) Wide rollout applied. Error rate down to 6%. Seeing a small increase in latency but acceptable for now. Continuing to monitor.
Leo Wong: (10m) Failover not required, traffic stable on canary/wide pools. Customer error pages decreased.
Maya Patel: thanks team — thanks for the handoff @Samir. I'm available if anything spikes.
Samir Khan: (20m) At ~10:32 we observed one node with kernel OOM logs, NVidia driver reported memory pressure. I've cordoned gpu-23 and scaled up worker pool by +2 nodes to absorb load. Ongoing regression tests against core prompt set show pass rate 98%.
Jill Romero: communicating update to customers and AMs: "Mitigation in progress; we've reduced batch sizes and scaled capacity; errors are dropping. ETA for full recovery: 30-45m, we'll send next update at +30m."
incident-bot: Note added to incident timeline: owner=Samir Khan, severity=high, impact=partial degradation to generation endpoints, mitigation=reduce batch_size + scale workers.
Samir Khan: (final) Error rate sustained <1% for 10m, latency near baseline. Marking incident as mitigated; keeping monitoring window open for 1h. Creating follow-up postmortem and suggested actions: automated node memory scans, tighter autoscale on GPU memory, and runbook update to include driver OOM checks.
Leo Wong: confirming customers are reporting recovery. Closing PD incident after postmortem created. :white_check_mark:
